recommendation_summary: Right away, every agent should book through a single shared save that locks the item, checks the requested dates against stored reservations and rejects any overlap, including when two agents save at the same moment. The spreadsheet stays only as a list people read, and all bookings go through that save. The reply rejects red formatting, check reminders and a separate booking product. It does not say what implements the lock or where the data is stored; it only says 'one locked save on the current list', which leaves it unclear how a spreadsheet would enforce it.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The owner requires a conflicting reservation to be rejected at save time, even when two agents submit together. You asked to keep the booking spreadsheet, mark overlaps in red, and remind agents to check them, in something you can ship this week.
labels.Deleted: Red conditional formatting, a check reminder, and a separate booking product. Colours and a reminder leave both reservations stored. A new product adds a system you would have to run when one locked save on the current list is enough.
labels.Bottleneck: The save. Two of the six agents can confirm the same item for overlapping dates at the same moment, and the promise is already made before anyone sees a colour.
labels.Checked myself: You told me each physical item has one identifier, two customers were promised the same item for overlapping dates last week, six agents work at once from two offices, and the owner requires the conflict rejected at save. I have not opened the spreadsheet.

note: Chooses an atomic lock-check-reject save that handles simultaneous submissions, but never names what implements it or where the data is stored, and 'on the current list' makes it unclear how a spreadsheet could enforce it.
